Cagliari and Udinese faced off in a crucial Serie A fixture on May 9, 2026, with both sides desperate to secure a defining result in the latter stages of the season. The atmosphere at the stadium was electric as the hosts looked to leverage their home advantage against a resilient visiting side. Early Pressure and VAR Intervention Cagliari dominated the opening exchanges, maintaining a staggering 62% of possession throughout the contest. Early attempts from outside the box by Juan Rodriguez and Michael Folorunsho signaled their intent, though neither could find the target. The match took a dramatic turn in the 33rd minute when the referee paused play for a lengthy VAR check regarding a potential penalty for the home side. Much to the frustration of the home crowd, the initial call stood, and no penalty was awarded, leaving the match scoreless as both teams headed into the tunnels at halftime. Clinical Counter and Defensive Heroics Shortly after the restart, Cagliari nearly took the lead when Sebastiano Esposito saw his goal-bound effort heroically hacked off the line by the Udinese defense. However, the momentum shifted in the 56th minute when the visitors struck against the run of play. A brilliant key pass from Oumar Solet released Hassane Kamara , who provided a pinpoint assist for Adam Buksa to tap home from close range. The goal forced Cagliari into a tactical reshuffle, bringing on veteran Andrea Belotti to bolster their attacking options. Stoppage Time Drama Seals the Win The closing stages were characterized by desperate Cagliari pressure and spectacular defending from Udinese . Alberto Dossena had a shot cleared off the line in the 76th minute, and Paul Mendy even attempted an audacious bicycle kick that flew wide. Despite the relentless onslaught, Udinese remained organized and struck a final blow in the 6th minute of stoppage time. Keinan Davis turned provider, setting up substitute Idrissa Gueye for a simple finish to double the lead. Led by a Man of the Match performance from Oumar Solet , the visitors navigated the final moments to secure a hard-fought away victory.

matches.description: Watch Lazio vs Udinese highlights and goals from Serie A on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on April 27, 2026. Lazio and Udinese locked horns in a high-stakes Serie A encounter that promised tactical intrigue and individual brilliance on the pitch. The atmosphere was electric as both sides looked to assert their dominance in a fixture often defined by narrow margins and late twists. Early Momentum and the Visitors' Surge The match, held on April 27, 2026 , began with a cagey opening as both sides searched for a rhythm. While Lazio attempted to control the tempo through possession, it was Udinese who struck the first blow in the 18th minute. A well-orchestrated move saw Jurgen Ekkelenkamp provide a precise delivery for Kingsley Ehizibue , who caught the defense stationary. Ehizibue met the ball with a perfectly timed right-footed volley that flew into the back of the net, silencing the home crowd and giving the visitors a precious lead. Following the opening goal, Lazio struggled to find an immediate answer. The first half grew increasingly physical, evidenced by a yellow card shown to Matteo Cancellieri for a reckless challenge. Despite several corners delivered by Tijjani Noslin and Toma Basic , the Udinese backline held firm. The visitors nearly doubled their lead through an Ekkelenkamp free kick, but the effort sailed wide, leaving the score at 1-0 heading into the break. Tactical Shifts and the Biancocelesti Fightback Lazio manager responded to the deficit by introducing Pedro and Fisayo Dele-Bashiru at the start of the second half, a move that immediately injected urgency into their play. The pressure paid off in the 50th minute when Luca Pellegrini produced a moment of magic. Following a corner sequence, Pellegrini found space to unleash a left-footed volley that beat Maduka Okoye , leveling the score at 1-1. The goal-scorer's joy was short-lived, however, as he soon found himself in the referee's book for unsportsmanlike conduct after a heated exchange. As the match entered the final ten minutes, the tactical battle intensified. In the 80th minute, Lazio appeared to have completed the comeback. Toma Basic found Pedro just outside the penalty area; the veteran Spaniard took a touch and unleashed a clinical right-footed strike from distance that nestled into the corner of the net. With the score at 2-1, the home fans celebrated what they believed was the winning moment, but the drama was only just beginning. A Frantic Finish at the Death Udinese refused to surrender and turned to their bench for inspiration, a move that bore fruit in the 86th minute. Substitute Arthur Atta found space in the box and expertly guided a left-footed shot past Edoardo Motta to restore parity. The visitors weren't finished yet. In the third minute of stoppage time, Vakoun Issouf Bayo played a pivotal role, setting up Atta for his second of the night. This time using his right foot, Atta completed a stunning turnaround to put Udinese 3-2 ahead, seemingly snatching all three points in the dying moments. However, the Olimpico had one final twist in store. In the 95th minute, Pedro turned provider, lofting a cross that found Daniel Maldini . The substitute controlled the ball and fired home a right-footed shot to make it 3-3. The goal was immediately subject to a lengthy VAR review for a potential infringement, but after several tense minutes, the referee confirmed the goal stood. Amidst the chaos, Patric received a yellow card for his role in the post-goal celebrations. The final whistle blew shortly after, concluding a breathtaking encounter where neither side could be separated despite a combined four goals in the final quarter-hour.

A pivotal Serie A encounter unfolded on 2026-05-24 as SSC Napoli hosted Udinese in a match that tested the resolve and tactical discipline of both squads. Fans at the stadium witnessed a battle where every inch of the pitch was contested, with momentum swinging between the two sides throughout the ninety minutes. Hoejlund Strikes as Napoli Dominate Possession From the opening whistle, SSC Napoli signaled their intent to control the tempo, utilizing their creative midfielders to carve out opportunities. An early header from Amir Rrahmani forced a comfortable save from Maduka Okoye , but the deadlock would not last long. In the 24th minute, a fluid attacking move saw Scott McTominay deliver a key pass to Kevin De Bruyne , who in turn provided the assist for Rasmus Hoejlund . The striker clinical finished with his right foot to put the hosts ahead. Udinese struggled to find a rhythm in response, often restricted to long-range efforts that failed to trouble Alex Meret . Napoli maintained a staggering 68% of the ball, dictating play and forcing the visitors into a defensive posture for much of the first half. While Matteo Politano and Eljif Elmas remained constant threats from distance, the visitors' defense held firm to prevent further damage before the interval. Red Card Drama and the Final Stand The complexion of the match shifted significantly in the 64th minute. After a VAR review for violent conduct, the referee upgraded a yellow card to a straight red card for Udinese defender Christian Kabasele . Facing a numerical disadvantage, the visitors introduced Adam Buksa and Idrissa Gueye to spark a late resurgence. Napoli responded with tactical substitutions of their own, including the introduction of Nikita Contini in goal and Pasquale Mazzocchi to shore up the flanks. In a frantic final sequence, Udinese threw everything forward, earning corners and testing the resolve of the Napoli backline. Juan Jesus and Billy Gilmour were forced into vital interceptions as the clock ticked down. Despite a late flurry of activity and shots from Idrissa Gueye and Branimir Mlacic being blocked, SSC Napoli held their nerve to secure the victory and all three points.
